extracted.subtask_description: A single database/profile entry summarizing the Snopes fact-checking website, including its claim-classification icons, operational metadata, methods, funding, and external evaluations. Useful for comparing verification tools or locating basic facts about Snopes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim classification icons
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes uses a number of icons to classify content: True, Mostly True, Mixture, Mostly False, False, Unproven, Outdated, Miscaptioned, Correct Attribution, Misattributed, Scan, and Legend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Icons are used to label the verdict or type of issue for content being evaluated; page does not provide detailed definitions for each icon beyond the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool type
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the primary purpose of the tool as verifying or assessing claims/content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the operational state of the tool at the time of cataloging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended users
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the target audience for the tool's outputs and interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denotes whether users must pay to access the tool's content or services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool focus
rubrics_metrics.description: This tool is content-focused. It directly evaluates information, such as the authenticity of a photo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the tool assesses content items (claims, images) rather than, for example, platform-level behaviors or network analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method or technology
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that evaluations are performed by people (rather than being automated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the tool automated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit yes/no flag indicating presence of automation; here the tool is not automated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founding organization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the organization that founded or operates the tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder / primary contact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names principal founders or contacts associated with the tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: How the tool addresses disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: This tool aims to fight disinformation by identifying, exploring, and correcting false information, giving people a resource for locating fact-based information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the tool's intended mechanism of impact: researching and correcting false claims and providing a fact-based resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection with tech platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes. Facebook uses Snopes as fact-checker for Facebook advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes any formal relationships with large platforms that affect the tool's reach or role in content moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding / revenue model
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how the tool is funded, which can bear on independence and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: External evaluations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assessment evaluates the tool's accuracy and objectivity, not the efficacy of the tool against disinformation; indicates external review of journalistic/fact-checking standards rather than impact metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database review/update status
rubrics_metrics.description: As of December 2020, Snopes is no longer being reviewed, and this page is not being updated with new data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that the entry is frozen as of a given date; relevant for currency and reliability of metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion in RAND database
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes was selected for this database because it fit our researchers' inclusion criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that selection was based on unspecified inclusion criteria used by the cataloging researchers.
